description.value: Live exchange is by patterned fluorescence of the cuticle under the primary, at a rate of some six figures a second, and durable claims are laid down in ground bract dye on the bark of a held span. The two halves are one system: a mark is read as a frozen utterance and is answered in flare, not in more marking. It carries ownership, rank and the terms of a dispute precisely, and has no way to state a past condition, so a scraped mark is simply a thing that was never true. The first survey spent four years recording the whole of it as decoration, which is what it looks like without a filter and, for that matter, with one.

sampleGloss.value: (three bars along the span, the outer bar broken) - span held, break at edge - this length is spoken for by the house, and the claim runs to the break and no further.

note.value: Recorded during elicitation and kept as the reference sample for this system.
